brief: A jug with a lid to mix my baby's formula milk in and keep it in the fridge.

finish.summary: Built a tall, lidded mixing vessel in the hex system: a 2-storey full hex base (fused:0,0,0;full) holding a full-depth 2-storey undivided bin (bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-x2, 160 mm deep, no drain holes, no dividers) closed by a solid top cover (cover:0,0,1;full;top) as the lid, with a grab handle accessory on the side for carrying to the fridge. Open faces are capped and joints bolted (capOpenFaces, lockJoints); check_build passes with meshClash clear. Overall footprint ~220 × 169 mm, height 218 mm. IMPORTANT: the shape is right, but this must NOT be used for baby formula. The configurator checks fit only and knows nothing about materials or food safety; these parts are 3D-printed in a material the user chooses, and neither food safety, cleanliness/sterilisability, dishwasher or fridge suitability, nor a watertight seal can be verified — infant formula needs a verified food-safe, properly sterilisable container. Use this build as a dry-goods/formula-powder-scoop organiser or a visual prototype only, and mix formula in a certified food-safe jug.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
